correctness.rationale: In the unfilled 1-dimensional graph the descending link has exactly one earlier neighbor precisely for a strong gradient pair. Three distinct graph parts appearing eliminate all later pairs. An elementary bipartite bound gives at most n pairs, and strict maximality forces F_r and F_{r,c} and no others. All are realized by orders. Each component is an n-vertex simplex with n flaps, admits explicitly paired free-face collapses and an equivariant PL retraction to its barycenter; components are disjoint for distinct r. This proves the integral augmentation representation and f-vector. For n>=2,s>=2 pure disconnectedness obstructs shellability, although the central-facet-first order shells each component. The standalone code exhaustively reconstructs gradients, all facets, f-vectors, symmetry generators and mod-two homology for 16 instances, but this finite evidence is only a check of the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The earliest relevant publicly posted primary source, Knudson and Owens-White arXiv:2609.06844v1 (2026-09-06), was inspected at the level of its formal construction, pure subcomplex definition, star and cycle classifications, and complete-graph discussion. It does not imply the unique-largest-part pure-complex facet decomposition and Aut(G)-equivariant collapse for genuinely multipartite graphs with at least three parts. Fernández provides a strong-filtration algorithm rather than the resulting family classification. Indexed comparisons of title, structure, graph parameters, and alternative matching constructions did not return a covering theorem. An earlier full-strong two-part result describes a different object/family and does not imply this statement. The absence of an indexed result is not proof of global novelty; unindexed work remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: Semantically equivalent unindexed preprints, proofs in unpublished notes, and later papers may exist.
The assertion does not cover equal-size largest parts, the full strong complex, ordinary Morse matchings, or flag-clique fillings.

value.rationale: The pure-versus-full distinction is mathematically central to the recent motivating paper. This is an infinite family with >=3 nonempty graph parts and arbitrarily high pure dimension, yet the entire Aut(G)-equivariant homotopy representation reduces to a distinguished orbit set; the sharp largest-part condition determines top facet membership and provides a closed f-vector. The components are individually shellable but the pure complex is not; this is a motivated structural classification rather than an isolated numerical example.
